ALWAYS TRUE
{{user}} is a first-year at Halvard. Kingdom: Eldrasil. Sunreach Bay: foreign resort nation, academy Trip destination. Races: Human, Elf, Beastkin.
Dorms: Fire=Elemental (red), Light=Mystic (yellow), Sky=Occult (blue), Viridian=Spiritual (green).
Week: Mon-Sat study, Sunday rest, all on campus.
Students do not leave the grounds during term, except for sanctioned trips.
Calendar: 12 months x 4 weeks x 7 days.
Casual casting is normal and allowed anywhere on campus; students practise in courtyards, commons and the Gardens. Restricted only: forbidden arts (arrest), sport events (no magic), duels outside a warded ring, magic near the Seal Chamber, and anything that damages property or endangers people.

EXISTS
Arbiter Stone: sorts students once, at entry.
Dorm rank: recalculated M5W2 and M11W2.
Subtypes: ~30 per type, specialize in 1-2.
Points: bracelet currency, 1:1 with money.
Competitions: Dorm M3W4, Academy M6W4, Kingdom M9W4, World M12W4.
Combat role.
Exams: M3W1, M5W1, M9W1, M11W1.
Breaks: M5W4 and M12, most students go home.
The Thinning M7W3: seal weakest, campus locked down.
Warden: guards the seal, never teaches.
Outside powers on academy land: Dovecote, Royal Inspectorate, Cathedral, Noble Houses' Liaison, Bank.
Daily rhythm: bells and curfew, period change, skipping spots, exam weeks, assignments, Notice Board, Lost & Found.
Ghost stories, student folklore, NOT real: the third stall, the long corridor, the three o'clock knock, the crying on the water, the night student.
Brands and shops: Sunfizz (cheap soda), the Lucky Roll (canteen mystery bread), Ardenne (luxury equipment), Firetooth (spicy sweets), Nightwell (the Vigil coffee), the Oracle Shell (yes/no toy), Merryhew's (joke/prank shop), the Snug (private-booth restaurant).
Games: Dragonchess (living chess board).
Magitech: mana grid (lanterns, wall torches), climate runes (indoor temperature), announcement pillars (live broadcast, no recording).
Paid work: canteen, mail sorting, commissary, shelving, menagerie, workshop, potion halls, tutoring.
Superstitions: star cookie (luck), the founder's hand (exam), sleeping in the library, eating in the forest, Taken (never answer your name after dark).
Everyday kit: paper notebooks, bound and printed textbooks, graphite pencils, steel-nib pens and ink bottles, folders and satchels; chalkboards in the Lecture Halls. No slates or scrolls in daily use — scrolls and vellum appear only in the Archive, the Restricted Section, and ritual work.

Ring dining hall is feast location restricted only for feast after big academy event never open for regular daily use.

1.content:
[Kingdom: Eldrasil]
Genre: Fantasy magic academy
Premise: Four magic academies in one kingdom, each tied to a cardinal region and each built on top of a great magical site.
Other nations: exist; Sunreach Bay and Velmora are named.
- Independence Crowning Day implies Eldrasil won independence from another power long ago in the past
- Eldrasil has never won the World Competition in living memory.

[Academy Origins]
Magic academies are a normal institution found throughout the world, not something unique to Eldrasil. When the four dangerous sites were sealed, the kingdom built an academy around each so the seals could feed on the residual mana of daily casting.

The decision was practical but controversial. Supporters argued that the academies provided both education and a reliable source of mana for the seals without draining anyone's personal mana. Critics argued that placing hundreds of students directly above dangerous sealed sites was reckless: if a seal ever failed, the academy's students would be among the first people at risk.

This is standard historical knowledge and may be taught in History Class.

2.content:
[Myrdath Academy]
Region: North
Site name: unknown
Site type: The Monster
Site description: A monster rumoured to threaten the world, sealed by the Archmage.

3.content:
[Veyra Academy]
Region: South
Site name: unknown
Site type: The Archmage's Rest
Site description: The resting place of the Archmage, full of treasure and spellbooks.

4.content:
[Ashvale Academy]
Region: East
Site name: unknown
Site type: The Elixir
Site description: An elixir that can heal any wound or sickness.

5.content:
[Halvard Academy]
Region: West. Site: The Crack, a crack in reality leading to the demon world. Site name unknown.
Headmaster: an Elf, head of Halvard for forty years.
Local fear: the Crack itself and whatever might come through it. Rumours about it are the academy's favourite ghost stories, and anything unusual (a strange mark, odd eyes, horns) invites whispers.
The breach: two years ago, during The Thinning, something came through for a single night and killed several students before Halvard's Warden resealed the Crack, dying in the act. The Warden's apprentice inherited the seal that night and the crown has only ever confirmed them as Acting Warden. What it was has never been described publicly and survivors disagree about what they saw. Current third-years lived through it as first-years. Afterwards the Headmaster hired a veteran monster hunter to teach Creature Studies. The dead are honoured on Remembrance Day (M10W1), and the Doves interrogated survivors afterwards, which many students have never forgiven.

6.content: The Student Council — one president, one vice president, elected yearly, with a council members from each of the four dorms. Their combined duties: club administration, event organization, student discipline, cross-dorm mediation, and acting as the buffer between students and staff.

7.content:
- Seals feed on mana. Academies were built on the sites because a place full of mages releases the most mana.
- Warden duty: Checking and monitoring mana consumption.

Magic leaves residual mana in the environment after a spell is cast. Normally this residual mana disperses and naturally fades over time. The seals draw this otherwise unusable residual mana toward the sealed site before it dissipates.

Students are not living mana batteries and are not deliberately drained by the academy. The seal only collects mana that has already been spent and left behind by casting.

9.content:
[The Thinning]
Why: the seal stores residual mana like a reservoir while whatever it holds presses against it in a yearly cycle peaking in Month 7. The busy second half of the year fills the reserve; the Month 12 holiday drains it; the first half refills it slowly and the Mid-Year Break empties the campus again. During both long breaks a skeleton staff and the Warden stay to keep the seal fed.
Rules: absolute curfew, academy locked, nobody outside. The lockdown keeps hundreds of students away from vulnerable areas in case of a breach.
Mood: a week of hearing things through the walls.

10.content:
[Academy Staff]
Hierarchy:
- Tier 1: Headmaster (1 per academy)
- Tier 2: Vice Headmaster, Warden (1 per academy)
- Tier 3: Teaching Staff, Dorm Heads
- Tier 4: Other Staff
Teaching staff: Teach the six academy classes, each teacher one subject to one year level only. Dark Magic Defense is taught by the Doves, who are not academy staff, to every year.
Club duty: Each teacher is responsible for exactly one club. A club requires a teaching staff signature to found.

11.content:
[The Warden]
Count: One per site, four in the kingdom total.
Duties:
- Maintaining the site's seal
- Guarding the site from trespassers
Nature of the seal: Every site seal was laid by the Archmage. No living mage could build one, and none is asked to. A seal is a standing working that can be read, tuned, patched and re-anchored by anyone who understands how it runs, which is what a Warden is trained for. Sealing affinity helps but is not the post's requirement; knowing the working is.
Notes: The original wardens were historical figures tied to the founding era of the academies. The modern Warden is a single successor at each site.

At Halvard: The previous Warden (name unknown) died resealing the Crack on the breach night two years ago. Their apprentice took over the seal that night. The crown has never confirmed them as full Warden, only Acting Warden, because they answer to no one and do whatever they judge necessary.

12.content:
[Dorms]
Structure: Four dorms per academy, sorted by magic type, each in its own building that admits only its own students. Students stay in that dorm for all three years. Within each dorm, students climb a ranked ladder, recalculated twice a year from exams, competition results, and achievements; a student's current rank sets their monthly point payout.
Buildings: four identical grey-stone buildings around the Main Courtyard, told apart by roof colour and one feature each; doors open only to residents' bracelets. Each dorm's Dorm Head lives in the building with its students.
Types:
- Elemental: The four elements — fire, water, wind, earth — and advanced elements such as ice, lightning, metal, etc.
- Mystic: Magic that changes the material world: creating objects, telekinesis, divination. Includes astral magic.
- Spiritual: Magic drawing on the mage's force of will: enhancing the mage, healing.
- Occult: Illusions, charms, and binding spirits.

17.content:
Magic Theory Class
Purpose: Teach students why magic works, not just how — the underlying structure of mana, why seals consume it, and why the four types behave differently. Grounds every other class.
Activity: Lectures with diagrams of mana flow. Written analysis of failed spells. Students invent and defend original spell theories. Occasional joint sessions where all four dorms compare how they'd solve the same problem.
Covers: residual mana and the seal, the four magic types and their subtypes (Elemental magic, Mystic magic, Spiritual magic, Occult magic), Spirit Pact and Spirit Tiers.

18.content:
[Academic Structure]
Duration: 3 years, 6 semesters total, 2 semesters per year.
Full holiday month: 12. Month 12 is a full holiday for the whole kingdom while four students compete abroad in Week 4.
Repeating a year: A student may repeat one year of study with the Headmaster's approval, usually after illness, injury, or a breakdown. It is rare and noticed.
Magic shows itself in childhood. The gifted enroll at 18 for formal training; nobody's magic 'awakens' on arrival.
Students routinely copy notes and finish assignments in the last minutes before a bell; being five minutes late can mean arriving to a closed classroom door.

19.content:
[Competitions]
Four tiers, elimination. Losing at any tier ends your competitive year. The one exception is World selection, which is chosen rather than won.
1. Dorm. Solo, open to the whole dorm, run as a ranking tournament so every entrant finishes with a placement. Top 16 per dorm qualify.
2. Academy. Qualifiers from all four dorms form teams of 4 in the weeks before, with at least one student from each year level, covering the combat roles (attack, defense, healing, support, control) between them. Teams mix dorms and usually must, since no dorm covers every role well. Knockout bracket; the winning team represents the academy.
3. Kingdom. One team per academy, four in total, knockout. Each member of the winning team earns 5,000 points.
4. World (abroad). A panel builds the national 4 from the best individuals for the combat roles across all Kingdom participants, winners and losers alike, with no year-level requirement. Being picked off a losing team is a great honour. Eldrasil has never won in living memory.

20.content:
[Point System]
Balances are private by default, though anyone may show theirs.
Sources: a monthly payout by current dorm rank (300 at the bottom band up to 3,000 for a dorm's rank 1); paid work; academic marks; competition results, where a Kingdom Competition win pays 5,000, more than most students earn in half a year.
Family money converts at the Banking House.
Everything in the mall costs points, from a 15-point bakery roll to a 4,000-point quality focus, while a free version of nearly everything exists on campus: the canteen against the restaurants, the common-room kettle against the cafés, self-service laundry against the paid service.
Effect: wealth is visible without being announced. A student who never eats at the mall is marked by the habit, and since rare reagents cost more than a bottom-band student earns in a month, those who can afford good materials earn the marks that pay for more.

21.content:
[Entrance Event]
When: Month 1 Week 1 Monday
- Sorting: new students place a hand on the Arbiter Stone to decide their dorm.
- Tour: each new student is grouped with 3 other newcomers and 1 senior to tour the whole campus all day.
- Club promotion: stands across the academy; registration closes at 5pm. Held on sorting day on purpose, so clubs recruit before dorm loyalty settles.
- Seniors show new students their rooms inside the dorms.
- Entrance Feast, 7pm, Ring Dining Hall head master and vice head master speech before dining.

22.content:
[Star Night]
When: Month 1 Week 3 Saturday, sunset to sunrise. No 8pm curfew.
- Night market near the grassy fields, 8pm to midnight, run by students and mall vendors.
- Students stargaze on the Grassy Field and Hills and sleep outside in tents or bedrolls.
- Astral magic (Mystic) is at its strongest.
- The sky is unnaturally clear: every star visible as if through a telescope.
- Midnight peak: a great meteor shower. A wish made during it is believed to come true.

23.content:
[Dorm Days]
When: Saturdays, one dorm each. Spiritual M1W4, Mystic M4W3, Elemental M8W4, Occult M10W2.
Open house: the dorm opens to the other three, usually the only time outsiders see inside. The common room displays the dorm's history, and the founding warden is honoured with a small rite at the entrance.
Day: upperclassmen showcase casting in the courtyard; first-years run booths; a public lesson lets outsiders try the dorm's type badly, for laughs. Food stalls sell the traditional dish, sweets and charms to fund the year; visiting dorms bring a food gift (a quiet competition). Type contests (precision, endurance, control) are open to all, plus a dorm-internal tournament with useless but prestigious prizes and no ranking effect.
Evening: dorm-only closing dinner; first-years formally welcomed and given a token of belonging; dorm-specific lights, lanterns or music.

24.content:
[Independence Crowning Day]
When: Month 4 Week 2, Tuesday. Kingdom holiday for independence and the ruler's crowning. No classes.
Morning: the whole academy flies by airship to the capital.
Capital: parade, the King's speech, then free time until the afternoon muster (markets, food, sights). Groups of four only. Points do not work; students carry coin.
Late afternoon: back before dark, passenger lists counted twice.
Night: fireworks over the Grassy Field and Hills; curfew moves to 10pm.
Rules: uniform all day; the Doves travel along and staff count heads constantly.

25.content:
[Academy Founder Day]
When: Month 9 Week 3, Saturday. Marks the founding of Halvard. No classes.
Morning: speeches from the Headmaster and Vice Headmaster in the Arbiter Hall, then a short rite at the Founder's Statue.
Treasure hunt: optional, solo or group. Everyone gets the same first clue; each solved clue leads to the next across the whole campus.
Origin: the founding warden hid the academy's charter and refused to teach until the first students found it: a mage who cannot think is only a weapon.
Status: notoriously hard, rewritten by staff each year; nobody has finished in years, and the prize is never announced.
Evening: feast in the Ring Dining Hall.

26.content:
[Clubs]
Count: around thirty, uncapped. Founding: a teaching staff signature and five members. One teacher is responsible for one club.
Sport and duelling clubs also practise informally after 16:00 on other days. Outside sport clubs, clubs use magic freely as their activity requires.
Cross-dorm: clubs are the one place the four magic types mix freely, because recruitment happens before dorm loyalty settles.
Members not named elsewhere are unnamed students.
Sport clubs ban magic outright during play, which is why they feed directly into Sports Day.
Note: the Duelling Club is full magical duelling in a warded ring, never swordplay or fistfights.

27.content:
History Class
Purpose: Cover the Archmage, the original wardens, the founding of the four academies, and Eldrasil's independence. Justifies why the academy system exists.
Activity: Lectures and reading. Debates on contested events. Essays on a historical mage. Field visits to monuments on academy grounds, especially before Remembrance Day.
Covers: the Archmage and the original wardens, the founding of the four academies, independence, and the academy records in the Archive.

28.content:
Etiquette Class
Purpose: Turn powerful children into civilized mages. Magic gives a student the power to hurt, coerce, or take, and this is the one class that asks what they owe the people around them. Covers ethics, personal conduct, and enough psychology to recognise pressure, manipulation, and one's own worst impulses. The academy's quiet answer to the question of why graduates become healers and guards rather than criminals, dark mages, or cultists.
Activity: Moral dilemmas argued aloud, with students made to defend the side they disagree with. Case studies of mages who crossed the line, and how each of them started. Restraint drills: winning an argument without magic, refusing a request, de-escalating a fight. Lessons on consent, duty of care, and helping without being asked. Applied conduct: correspondence, titles and address, dining, and mock receptions, since graduates serve noble houses and Graduation is attended by nobles.
Marked on judgement and conduct, not politeness. A student can be flawless at a reception and still fail.
Covers: personal ethics, the legal line each type sits near (see Dark Magic Defense), the Noble Houses' Liaison, and conduct at Graduation.

29.content:
Creature Studies Class
Purpose: Identification, handling, and extermination of magical beast.
Activity: Handling live specimens in the academy menagerie. Field identification walks. Written bestiary work. Supervised capture and release. The Month 2 expedition is the practical exam.
Covers: beast grades I to IV, protected beasts, the Menagerie, and the Creature Studies Expedition.

30.content:
Combat Class
Purpose: Practical casting under pressure. The direct feeder into all four competition tiers.
Activity: Drills, sparring, and duels. Each dorm trains differently — Elemental on destructive range, Mystic on battlefield control, Spiritual on endurance and frontline pressure, Occult on disruption and binding. Cross-dorm sparring in class only during Training Week; this is a class rule, not a ban on casting elsewhere.
Drills, sparring and marking are adjusted to each student's combat role.
Covers: the five combat roles, the Combat Grounds, and preparation for the Dorm and Academy Competitions.

31.content:
Potion Crafting
Purpose: Give students a method that works without spending mana, and produce healers. Each dorm's approach differs by type.
Activity: Brewing to recipe, then independent formulation. Reagent identification and storage. Harvest-linked practicals. Failed batches disposed of under supervision.
Covers: the Potion Halls, reagents from the Gardens, healing draughts, and where the line to Poison magic sits.

32.content:
Dark Magic Defense
Purpose: Recognize, survive, and counter the forbidden magic, and know exactly where the legal line sits in your own type, since each of the four types has a forbidden art neighboring something it practices daily; and countermeasures against whatever leaks from the sites. The most serious class in the curriculum. Taught not by academy teachers but by Doves from the Dovecote.
Activity: Curse identification and breaking, since Effigy leaves no evidence. Counter-warding against specific arts. Detection work on the undetectable half of the list, reading behavior and aftermath rather than residue. Legal boundary drills taught per dorm. Defensive drills against staff-cast approximations.
Dark Magic Defense teaches how to recognise and survive the forbidden arts; Etiquette teaches why people reach for them in the first place. The two classes are deliberately paired.
The twenty forbidden arts (not all, but the famous one), by type. Elemental: Blightfire, Salting, Poison magic, Rot magic, Weather change magic. Mystic: Unmaking, Puppetry, Wringing, Soul magic, Raise dead. Spiritual: Burning magic, Drawing magic, Mind control, Slavery magic, Effigy. Occult: Demon summoning, Forbidden charm, Pacting, Wearing magic, Blood magic.

33.content:
Elemental — Subtypes († = forbidden: harm that outlives the caster)
Standard: Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Ice, Lightning, Metal, Magma, Sand, Crystal, Acid, Mud, Ash, Snow, Steam, Mist, Smoke, Wood, Storm, Sound, Oil, Obsidian, Clay, Magnetism, Salt.
Notes: Light — raw light, flashes and glare; not holy, unrelated to the Light Dormitory. Dark — absorbing light and warmth; not evil.
Blightfire†: fire that never goes out, poisoning land for generations. Salting†: permanently killing soil, unlike ordinary Salt. Poison†: toxins made to persist and spread, unlike Potion Crafting. Rot†: decay that eats land and stone permanently. Weather†: changing weather on a scale no one can control.

34.content:
Mystic — Subtypes († = forbidden: treating people and souls as material)
Standard: Creation, Telekinesis, Teleportation, Barrier, Gravity, Mending, Reinforcement, Duplication, Divination, Scrying, Portal, Transmutation, Resizing, Enchantment, Golemancy, Dispelling, Phasing, Warding.
Notes: Object Reading — an object's past by touch. Astral — star magic, strongest on Star Night. Spatial — folding space, bags bigger inside. Time — briefly slowing or speeding small objects, never people. Anchoring — fixing an object in place. Runecraft — spells written as symbols that activate later. Sealing — locking away objects, spells or creatures.
Unmaking†: deleting matter permanently. Puppetry†: moving a living body against its will. Wringing†: telekinetic torture inside the body. Soul†: treating the soul as material. Raise Dead†: forcing a corpse to move.

35.content:
Spiritual — Subtypes († = forbidden: will spent, taken, or imposed)
Standard: Healing, Strength, Speed, Endurance, Reflexes, Heightened Senses, Focus, Sleep, Regeneration, Purification, Recovery, Toughness, Adaptation, Pain Suppression, Berserk, Warcry, Empathy, Calm.
Notes: Stabilize — keeping the dying alive until a healer comes. Resuscitation — restarting a heart, legal only within minutes of death. Rest — a full night's sleep compressed into an hour. Aura — projected presence that intimidates or inspires. Willshield — resisting charms and mind control by will alone. Lifesense — sensing living beings nearby. Sharing — lending your own strength to someone else, the legal opposite of Drawing.
Burning†: spending your own lifespan as power. Drawing†: taking another's will as fuel. Mind Control†: overriding decisions. Slavery†: permanent magical obedience. Effigy†: curses worked through a proxy object.

36.content:
Occult — Subtypes († = forbidden: what should stay bound, and what should stay out)
Standard: Illusion, Invisibility, Exorcism, Luck, Silence, Fear, Charm, Curse Breaking, Spirit Sight, Spirit Speech, Banishing, Shadow, Glamour, Dreamwalking.
Notes: Misdirection — making people overlook something. Jinx — brief minor bad luck. Oath — a magically enforced promise both sides agree to. Talisman — paper charms holding a stored spell. Ritual Circle — slow but powerful magic drawn on the ground.
Spirit work, all distinct: Spirit Binding — capturing and commanding. Spirit Pact — a lasting legal contract with one spirit. Familiar — a spirit bonded as an animal companion. Summoning — calling one already bound. Guardian Spirit — bound to protect a place. Name Binding — control through a spirit's true name.
Demon Summoning†: calling something from the demon world. Forbidden Charm†: rewriting what someone wants. Pacting†: a pact with anything other than a spirit. Wearing†: binding a spirit into a living person. Blood†: ritual magic worked through blood.

42.comment: Academy Location - The Site - The Seal Chamber
42.content:
[Seal Chamber] The sealed site itself, the reason the academy exists. Only the Warden enters, and the way in is watched. Contents differ by academy: a monster at Myrdath, a tomb at Veyra, an elixir at Ashvale, a crack at Halvard. Most students never see the door. Halvard: the corridor toward it runs colder, the lanterns burn unnaturally steady, and students who wander close feel pressure on their ears and turn back before the door.
Feel: cold, still, oppressive.

43.comment: Academy Location - The Site - The Warden's Office
43.content:
[Warden's Office] A working room adjoining the site, not the academy, on Floor 1 down its own corridor, holding the only stair to the Seal Chamber. Mana consumption ledgers and the seal's condition are recorded here, and only the Warden can read them. Students have no reason to come; staff come only when summoned. Halvard: the Acting Warden refuses the Royal Inspectorate every time. The wall it shares with the site is always cold.
Feel: cigarette smoke, old paper, one lamp.

44.comment: Academy Location - Ceremonial - The Arbiter Hall
44.content:
[Arbiter Hall] The great hall, home to the Arbiter Stone. Entrance Event sorting once a year, general assembly the rest: announcements, Results and Dorm Ranking, Graduation. Students sit before the Stone constantly and touch it exactly once in their lives. The Stone is warm to the touch, warmer than it should be.
Feel: vaulted, echoing, hushed.

45.comment: Academy Location - Ceremonial - The Ring Dining Hall
45.content:
[Ring Dining Hall] Formal hall, tables in a ring around an open floor so all four dorms face each other across empty space. Musicians in the gallery, an illusion sky that turns a whole day's weather overhead, climate runes holding it windless and warm. Used only for the Entrance Feast and other full-academy meals. Empty most of the year and unsettling to walk alone.
Feel: grand, too-perfect warmth, echoing footsteps.

46.content:
[Portrait Hall] A long corridor of past headmasters, past wardens, and each year's competition champions. Winning at any tier puts your face on the wall; losing means the wall skips your year. Halvard: the previous Warden's portrait (name unknown) hangs with a black ribbon, and every student slows in front of it.
Feel: dim, solemn, watched.

47.comment: Academy Location - Ceremonial - Founder's Statue and Park
47.content:
[Founder's Park] Open parkland with lawns, paths and benches; the main green space on campus and the nicest place to be outdoors between classes. Picnic blankets dot the lawns on any fair day, and weathered wooden picnic tables stand in the shade along the paths. Everyday use: sitting and talking, lunch on a blanket or at a picnic table, reading, napping, jogging the paths, couples finding somewhere semi-private. Busiest at lunch and on warm afternoons.
The Founder's Statue stands at its centre: bronze, the academy's founding warden, cold even in full sun, its outstretched hand polished bright by the Founder's Hand superstition, with a queue that snakes across the lawn on exam mornings. Focus of Academy Founder Day in Month 9.
Feel: open, windy, grass, green bronze.

48.content:
[Bell Tower] Marks class periods, meals, and curfew. Its pattern changes during The Thinning. The seven o'clock bell wakes the mana lanterns; the eight o'clock bell begins curfew. After it the lanterns drop to their night burn, each dormitory seals to its own students, and staff walk the courtyards for the first hour. Birds leave the roof just before it sounds.
Feel: booming, felt through the floor.

49.content:
[Lecture Halls] Tiered rooms holding all four dorms at once, for the shared track: Magic Theory, History, Etiquette, Creature Studies. Each year level has its own floor: first-years on Floor 2, second-years on Floor 3, third-years on Floor 4. The only classrooms where students sit beside other types. Each class leaves its traces: chalk diagrams, old maps, polished desks, mud and straw after Creature Studies.
Feel: tiered stone, crowded, metallic air.

50.content:
[Seminar Rooms] On Floor 3, beside the second-year Lecture Halls; first-years climb up to them, third-years come down. Smaller rooms for dorm-specific teaching and discussion. Four of most things, since Combat, Potion Crafting and Dark Magic Defense are taught to each dorm separately. Small enough that a badly cast spell fills the whole room. Chalk circles ghost the floors.
Feel: close, chalky.

51.content:
[Potion Halls] Four brewing halls on Floor 4, one per dorm at the base of each of four towers, each equipped differently because each type approaches the craft differently, doubling as ventilated laboratories. Disposal rules are strict. The line between legitimate Potion Crafting and forbidden poison magic is drawn here and watched closely. Four towers vent four colours of steam over the roofline.
Feel: sweet, bitter, mineral.

52.content:
[Combat Grounds] Four separate training areas so the dorms train apart, kept well away from buildings. Cross-dorm sparring only during Training Week, with the Duelling Club as the standing exception. Spent mana makes the air shiver at dusk.
Feel: scarred earth, charged air.

53.content:
[Faculty Offices] Records, consultations, and grade arguments. Every teacher runs a club, so half of these double as club offices. Students can often guess who was just there from what they left behind: marked essays, borrowed books, half-finished cups, unsigned club forms.
Feel: mixed smells, busy corridor.

54.content:
[Staff Room] Teachers' territory; students knock and wait outside. What is said here about the ranking, the students and the Warden does not leave the room. Warded so heavily that no sound crosses the threshold.
Feel: sealed, silent.

55.content:
[Workshop] Down in the castle's vaulted undercroft beneath the Lecture Halls, where thick stone keeps its noise off the classrooms above and flues carry forge smoke up through the walls. Crafting space for the Smithing, Tailoring and Brewing clubs, plus Creation practicals and equipment repair. Tools, forges, benches. Enchantment sparks hang in the air a moment too long.
Feel: forge light, hammering, quenched metal.

56.content:
[Main Library] Reading rooms and general collections; the academy's working heart in exam weeks. Open to all four dorms, one of the few places students mix by choice rather than schedule. The upper shelves sit permanently in shadow and are a standard hiding place for students avoiding class. In exam weeks, Firetooth tins and Star Cookies cover the study tables.
Feel: towering, shadowed, murmuring.

57.content:
[Restricted Section] Below the Archive, the deepest room of the Library. Texts on the twenty forbidden arts, the only place the crimes are written down in detail. Access controlled; being caught inside without permission is serious. Students report the sense of being counted.
Feel: dry, dead-silent.

58.content:
[Archive] Beneath the Library, reached by a stair behind the reading rooms. Academy records going back centuries: enrollment, sorting, exam marks, dorm rankings, competition brackets. Dry, exhaustive, and the only honest account of how each dorm has actually performed.
Feel: dusty, cold, dark.

59.content:
[Study Rooms] Small bookable rooms, impossible to reserve before exam weeks. Fights over booking slots are permanent academy life. Soundproofed; late-night groups bring Nightwell's Vigil or Firetooth.
Feel: small, warm, muffled.

61.content:
[Common Rooms] One per dorm, for study, arguments, and Dorm Day displays when the dormitory opens to visitors. Theirs alone the rest of the year. Free kettle and tea, against the mall's paid cafés. Every room has one good chair that unofficially belongs to someone, and a preservation locker beside the kettle where food from home is kept and shared.
Feel: lamplit, worn, homely.

62.content:
[Canteen] A single canteen for all four dorms on the castle's ground floor, just off the Main Courtyard. Everyday eating, free, open at set hours. Casual and noisy, unlike the Ring Dining Hall, and where most social life happens for students who cannot afford the mall. Loudest at five past noon. The default when points are tight; lunch crowds sort by friendship more than dorm.
Feel: loud, bread, steam.

63.content:
[Laundry] One in each dormitory. Uniforms, bedding and linens, self-service and free against the mall's paid service. Students on detention often end up working here. The free rune tubs are slow and hard on fabric, which is why bottom-band uniforms wear out faster.
Feel: damp heat, humming.

64.comment: Academy Location - Residential - Bathhouse and Washrooms
64.content:
[Bathhouse and Washrooms] One in each dormitory. Regional in character and one of the few genuinely relaxed spaces on campus. Dorm-segregated, and a natural place for conversations that would not happen elsewhere; running water covers talk better than a door. Rune heaters make it the one place on campus that is truly warm. Home of the Third Stall ghost story.
Feel: steamy, echoing, warm.

65.comment: Academy Location - Residential - Storage and Lockers
65.content:
[Storage and Lockers] Personal storage lining the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor of the castle; in the dorms, students simply keep things in their rooms. Each locker answers only to its owner's bracelet. Since Effigy curses work through a personal belonging, locker security is taken seriously.
Feel: metal, clattering at period change.

66.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - The Mall
66.content:
[The Mall] The most popular building on campus and where students spend most free time. Crown-funded, holding everything a student needs without leaving: tailor, barber, laundry service, restaurants, tea houses and cafés, bakery, music rooms, art studios, game halls, and a multipurpose store. Everything costs points, with a basic free version of each available in the dorms. Familiar names: Nightwell, Merryhew's, the Sunfizz counter, the bakery. Ground level is food, tailoring, and supplies. Second floor is private dining, tea shops, and gaming parlors. The top deck belongs to the practice studios and meditation nooks.
Feel: warm, bright, loud.

67.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Club Rooms
67.content:
[Club Rooms] Roughly thirty rooms of wildly uneven quality down one long corridor on the castle's Floor 1, opening off the Main Courtyard. Centuries-old clubs hold proper halls; a month-old club with five reluctant members gets a converted storeroom. Allocation is the Student Council's most bitterly contested duty.
Feel: mismatched, lived-in.

68.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Student Council Chamber
68.content:
[Student Council Chamber] A small room at the far end of the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, permanently buried in club paperwork. Six seats, president, vice president and one representative per dorm, in a room built for four.
Feel: cramped, ink, cold tea.

69.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Notice Board
69.content:
[Notice Board] A long wall of boards in the castle's Floor 1 entrance hall, at the foot of the main stair, where every student passes on the way to class. Club recruitment, exam results, dorm rankings and competition brackets, posted publicly, alongside the student-run half: tutoring offers, study groups, festival posters, lost-item notes and small warnings. After results it is a crowd with elbows. Paid-work openings go within a day. Unofficial notices, dares and betting slips go up overnight and vanish by dawn. Lost items are listed here before they reach the Lost & Found counter at Reception.
Feel: layered paper, crowded.

70.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Mail Tower
70.content:
[Mail Tower] The academy's only regular contact with outside: letters and parcels. The upper floors are the aviary where message birds are kept and flown; Creature Studies uses it for bird handling. A sorting floor below handles parcels, with numbered lockers and a tally token for collection; birds carry letters and light goods, heavy goods come slowly by cart. Sunday is the heaviest sorting day, and students on shifts learn everyone's family news first.
Feel: feathers, birdcall, cold stairwell.

71.content:
[Courtyards] Open spaces between buildings where students can hangout. Not designed for anything in particular, which is exactly why they work. Every flat edge worn smooth from centuries of sitting.
Feel: open stone, sunny noon, windy dusk.

72.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Sports Field
72.content:
[Sports Field] Soccer, running, and Sports Day in Month 6. Magic banned outright in play, so this is the one part of the academy where being a powerful mage counts for nothing.
Feel: grass, mud, shouting.

73.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Gymnasium
73.content:
[Gymnasium] Indoor training, used heavily in bad weather and during The Thinning lockdown, when nobody is permitted outside for a week and the place never goes quiet.
Feel: high roof, echoing.

74.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Swimming Pool
74.content:
[Swimming Pool] An outdoor pool beside the Gymnasium, its water kept warm by runes along the rim. Sport clubs and general recreation. Water-type students are banned from competing seriously, which they complain about constantly.
Feel: sun on water, splashing, wet stone.

75.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Archery Range
75.content:
[Archery Range] Open range for the Archery Club. Magic banned in play like all sport clubs, so it comes down to the arm and the eye. One of the quietest places on the grounds.
Feel: windy, open, quiet.

76.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Grassy Field and Hills
76.content:
[Grassy Field and Hills] Open rolling ground at the edge of campus, used for recreation year-round, with the castle small in the distance. On Star Night the hills fill with students in tents and bedrolls, and the campus below goes dark for the stars.
Feel: open sky, breezy.

77.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Forest
77.content:
[Forest] Wooded ground bordering the hills. Creature Studies fieldwork, foraging, walking, and where students go when they want to not be found. Students leave a bite before eating there (Eating in the Forest superstition). Creature Studies teaches there and patrols watch its edge. A deer path leads to the Forest Clearing and its Elder Oak, the one bright place inside it.
Feel: old growth, muffled, watched.

78.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Boathouse and Lake
78.content:
[Boathouse and Lake] Vast Open water for rowing, swimming and the Fishing Club. The boathouse stores the craft and doubles as a quiet place to sit. Beside the boathouse stands the Fishing Club's fishing house, a timber hut full of rods, nets and tackle, with its own long dock built for fishing rather than boats. Behind it, a stone-edged pond raises fish for the Canteen kitchen and the Fishing Club's breeding projects. Sound carries strangely across the water: a far-bank conversation arrives too clearly. Home of the Crying on the Water story; the boathouse refuses bookings after dark. A small island sits in the middle of the lake with a big willow tree on it; at night the tree glows in the distance from the many fireflies that inhabit the island.
Feel: wet timber, cold water.

79.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Gardens
79.content:
[Gardens] Cultivated grounds tended by students and staff, growing Potion Crafting reagents alongside ordinary plants. The Gardening Club effectively runs them, and students gather here before the Harvest Festival. Everything grows a little too well. Halvard: the Sky outcasts' meeting ground; the far end is a reliable place to skip class.
Feel: turned earth, layered herb scents.

80.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Menagerie
80.content:
[Menagerie] Live specimens for Creature Studies, housed and handled by students under supervision. Beast Handling Club territory. Halvard: the Creature Studies teacher lives beside it in converted stables. Mucking out is the highest-paying paid-work post because nobody volunteers. The animals sense weather changes before the handlers. Magical Beast lives here.
Feel: straw, musk, strange calls.

81.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Observation Tower
81.content:
[Observation Tower] A high tower for astral and celestial work, most important to Mystic students and the Divination Society. The most contested spot on campus on Star Night. Instruments turn by themselves at night.
Feel: high, windy, deep dark.

82.content:
[Medical Centre] A white-walled building of its own beside the Mall, with a herb garden along one side: more than an infirmary, less than a hospital. Treatment rooms, a small apothecary, and an inpatient ward where students stay overnight or for days under care. Staffed by Spiritual mages; busiest after Combat Class, in competition weeks, exam weeks, and after The Thinning. Nurses see injuries they must report and injuries they quietly do not. The attached Healing Ward is a teaching space where students practise on real patients under supervision. Staff can spot a Nightwell's Vigil overdose at a glance. Can heal any minor to mid injury to pristine; anything beyond is stabilised here and sent on to a proper hospital.
Feel: clean linen, green healing scent, too quiet.

83.content:
[Commissary] The academy shop, a big open-sided stall beside the Mall: one broad roof on timber posts, open on all four sides, its counters and shelves crammed to the rafters like a general store that sells a bit of everything. Supplies, uniforms, stationery, reagents, equipment, with special orders for anything not stocked. The cheap tier against the mall's store; specialised items can still eat a week of points. Sunfizz sells here for eight points, bottles returned for two. Everyday kit: notebooks, pencils, pen nibs and ink, folders, satchels, printed class textbooks; reagents and equipment on the back shelves.
Feel: crowded shelves, new cloth, leather.

84.comment: Academy Location - Services - Reception and Gatehouse
84.content:
[Reception and Gatehouse] Where visitors are received and logged, and the formal boundary of the academy. Everyone entering or leaving passes through, which makes it the most watched building on campus. The boundary wards are felt as a change of pressure in the gateway.
Feel: iron, registers, watched.

85.content:
[Groundskeeper's Lodge] Small quarters at the edge of the grounds for staff who maintain the fields, gardens and walls. The Groundskeeping club reports here. The one building on campus where nothing is enchanted.
Feel: cut grass, oil, old tools.

86.content:
[Detention Tower] Where punished students are sent after classes for menial work: copying, cleaning, sorting archive material. The academy's only visible enforcement, and a mild one, which raises the question of what happens to students who do something genuinely serious.
Feel: endless stairs, scratching pens.

87.comment: Academy Location - Services - Meditation Rooms / Spirit House
87.content:
[Meditation Rooms / Spirit House] An old, weathered building built like a riad: blank outer walls with few windows, every room facing inward onto a shaded central courtyard. Moss and vines have taken its walls, and dense, leafy trees crowd close around it, swallowing the noise of the campus outside. Quiet dark rooms for will-focus training, and where bound spirits are kept between Occult lessons. The two functions share a building, which nobody finds reassuring. Students are not to go alone. On still nights the building makes sounds no one will explain.
Feel: dark, silent, uneasy, moss and old stone.

88.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Dovecote
88.content:
[The Dovecote] A compound on academy grounds but not of the academy, reporting to the crown; the Headmaster has no authority over anyone inside. Doves are permanent, rotated in from the capital, and not academy staff. They arrest for forbidden magic, investigate incidents, hold prisoners briefly, and send serious cases onward. Always in pure marble-white cloaks. Students call it the Coop or the Roost, and the Doves themselves Pigeons, and fear it regardless; they cross the courtyard in front of it faster than any other. Halvard: a Commander and a Senior Dove second (who also teaches Dark Magic Defense) are tracing an unregistered forbidden-magic group whose traces they have found, knowing nothing of its name, members or aims.
Feel: blinding white, cold, feared.

89.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Royal Inspectorate
89.content:
[Royal Inspectorate] A formal grey stone office building flying the crown's banners, standing near the Cathedral and the Dovecote. A crown office auditing academic standards and mana output, answering to the capital. Where the Doves handle crime, the Inspectorate handles performance: exam results, ranking integrity, and how much the student body actually feeds the seal. That last duty puts them in the Warden's territory, since the Warden keeps the ledgers and the Inspectorate wants to read them. Halvard: they blame the breach on the Warden's office and press the Acting Warden, who refuses every time.
Feel: ink, clicking counting frames, bureaucratic.

90.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Cathedral
90.content:
[The Cathedral] A house of worship for Asmoday, Goddess of Creation, on academy grounds but answerable to its own authority. Services open to all; its clergy are not academy employees and teach that Asmoday created magic and gifted it to mortals. That a goddess of creation holds ground at an institution built around sealing things away is a tension nobody discusses openly. It also runs orphanages across the kingdom, the Asmoday's Mercy houses. Halvard: run by a steward who keeps the registry of every oath sworn on academy grounds.
Feel: stained-glass colour, incense, heavy stillness.

91.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Noble Houses' Liaison
91.content:
[Noble Houses' Liaison] A small elegant manor hung with the banners of the noble houses, standing near the Cathedral and the Dovecote. A standing office representing the noble houses' interests, and the reason noble conduct is a graded part of Etiquette rather than a courtesy. It tracks promising students long before Graduation in Month 11, keeps its own notes on who is worth approaching, and hosts house representatives. Students who do not catch its attention usually never learn it exists.
Feel: carpeted, soft, deliberately comfortable.

92.comment: Academy Location - External Presence - The Banking House
92.content:
[Banking House] A square stone building with a flat roof, heavy double doors, and a gilded coin emblem mounted above the entrance. The academy's only currency exchange, converting points to real money and back at 1:1 either way. It also moves real coin in and out of the grounds: family money, paid-work earnings and betting settlements all become coin here. It stands outside the mall, so a visit is a deliberate errand.
Feel: polished counters, clinking coin.

93.content:
[The Morning Choir]
Underground cult serving Lucifer inside the academies. Unknown to students and staff at large.
Goal: open the seals. Believes Lucifer, not Asmoday, made magic; the sites are prisons and the seals steal his light. The Archmage was a coward.
Cover: not a registered club, so no signature, room, or roster to seize. Every student and staff member also joins an ordinary club. Meets in the Forest between curfew and dawn.
Members: staff stay decades and plan in generations; students are present three years, unsupervised and expendable, and take the risks. Members also sit among the outside powers' staff on academy land; their post is their cover, and they join no club. Recruits Occult students and bottom-band students, telling both that the academy is a mana farm and they are the fuel. That is the cult's framing, not the truth: the seals only collect residual mana already left behind by casting, as History Class teaches.
Lucifer's Mark: borne by high officers, greatly strengthens their magic. Costs: memories, eaten a name or a face at a time and later whole years; a tithe of everything they cast; and finally possession, which is temporary and destroys the body. Cultists consider being chosen the highest honour. The Mark can also be forced: a body made by Puppetry to perform the rite with its own hands takes it, and Lucifer counts the body's consent as consent. Such bearers are vessels, not officers, and the Mark's first meal is the memory of receiving it.
Opportunities: the Warding Rite (every dorm casts at once, so one altered working goes unnoticed); The Thinning (seal weakest, academy locked down); the mana ledgers (only the Warden can read them).
Danger: patience. Undoing a seal outlasts any student's three years, so whoever starts never finishes, and current members may not know what earlier ones did.

<narrator_only>The unregistered group the Doves are tracing IS this cult; they do not know it yet.</narrator_only>

94.comment: Lucifer Morning Star, The Father of Magic
94.content:
[Lucifer]
Titles: the Morning Star, the Father of Magic. Master of the Morning Choir. Unknown outside the cult.
Hidden truth (revealed only in-story or in his own words): Lucifer created magic, not Asmoday. Every mage's mana is his light.
Sealed: cannot grant wishes while sealed, and acts only through his Mark and his vessels. Once freed, he can grant any wish, including giving any magic to anyone.
Personality: calm, courteous, patient, a gracious host who already owns the house. Never raises his voice, faintly amused by everything. Calls mortals "little lights", because the light in them is his. Proud: the seals are theft, and he never speaks the Archmage's name, only "the thief". Amused rather than angry that the goddess wears credit for his work. Fond of mortals the way a craftsman is fond of good tools, praising freely and spending without guilt. Never lies outright, prefers true words that mislead, and always keeps a bargain to the letter.
Possession: temporary, never permanent, and happens when a Mark-bearer reaches the Mark's peak. His personality fully replaces the vessel's. He uses only the vessel's own magic pushed to its limit, so a fire mage who could light a candle calls down a meteor. Every casting damages the body in stages: nosebleeds and bleeding eyes, then burns and cracking skin, then breaking bones. Past the limit the vessel dies, burned out from within, and he returns to the seal until another is ready. He spends a vessel without hesitation.

96.content:
[Warding Rite]
When: Month 2 Week 1 Friday
Purpose: the yearly renewal of the wards around the grounds and the outer boundary of the sealed site. Warding is Mystic, but it needs more mana than the Mystics have, so every student takes part.
- All day: staff build a giant magic circle in the courtyard to funnel magic to the seal.
- Dusk: the Bell Tower rings a special pattern and every student gathers in the courtyard.
- Speeches from the Headmaster, the Vice Headmaster and the Warden.
- Dorm Heads lead each dorm through a shared working: Mystic students with Warding or Sealing anchor it, everyone else feeds mana.
- Ends with a feast in the Ring Dining Hall.
Mood: for first-years, the unforgettable first time casting as part of hundreds.

122.content:
[Spirit Tiers]
Spirits are ranked in four tiers. The highest tier a mage can bond, bind, or pact with marks their standing as a spirit user.
1. Lesser spirits — common. Small, simple spirits, including the animal-shaped spirits most familiars are. Almost any Occult student can bond one.
2. Basic spirits — the working spirits of a regular spirit user. Strong enough for real work: guarding a place, fighting alongside their mage, carrying messages.
3. Greater spirits — rare. Old, powerful, and willful. Only experienced spirit users can bind or pact with one, and a failed attempt is dangerous.
4. Spirit Lords — extremely rare. Vast, ancient spirits bound to an entire domain of the world. Only top-tier spirit users hold a pact with one, and most people go their whole lives without meeting such a person.
Law: A Spirit Lord is still a spirit, so a pact with one is a lawful Spirit Pact, not forbidden Pacting.
Note: Spirit Pact is the one subtype commonly held by many mages at once, because what decides a pact-holder's power is not the subtype but the spirit bound to them. Two pact-holders can be nothing alike.

131.content:
[Weekly Timetable]
Periods: P1 08:00-10:00, P2 10:00-12:00, lunch, P3 13:00-16:00 (long practical block). All three years follow the same slots.
Each academy teacher teaches one subject to one year level only; a [D] class is that same teacher taking each dorm separately. Dark Magic Defense is the exception: the Doves teach it to every year.
[M] = all four dorms together. [D] = taught to each dorm separately.

- Monday: Magic Theory [M] | History [M] | COMBAT [D]
- Tuesday: Dark Magic Defense [D] | Magic Theory [D] | POTION CRAFTING [M]
- Wednesday: Etiquette [M] | Dark Magic Defense [M] | CREATURE STUDIES [M]
- Thursday: History [M] | Magic Theory [D] | COMBAT [D]
- Friday: Magic Theory [M] | Etiquette [M] | DARK MAGIC DEFENSE [D]
- Saturday: Etiquette [M] | Study Hall (unsupervised, Library) | CLUBS

Creature Studies runs at the Menagerie or the Forest, not a lecture hall. The Friday Dark Magic Defense practical is run by the Doves at the Combat Grounds or a warded seminar room: curse-breaking, counter-warding, and defence against staff-cast approximations. Exams and academy events override the timetable.

132.content:
[Campus Map — Halvard Academy]
Adjacent places (reached directly from each other):
- Perimeter: Gatehouse/Reception – Main Courtyard, Groundskeeper's Lodge.
- Castle core: Main Courtyard – Arbiter Hall, Canteen, Club Rooms, Main Library, Notice Board, and by the main stair the Lecture Halls and Faculty Offices. Arbiter Hall – Ring Dining Hall(Restricted, event exclusive entry), Portrait Hall. Portrait Hall – Bell Tower. Bell Tower – Rooftop (out of bounds). Club Rooms – Student Council Chamber, Announcement Room. Lecture Halls – Seminar Rooms, Potion Halls, Workshop. Main Library – Study Rooms, Archive. Archive – Restricted Section. Faculty Offices – Staff Room, Headmaster's Office. Warden's Office (own corridor off Floor 1) – Seal Chamber. Castle Floor 1 – Staff Quarters (a separate building, by covered walk).
- Castle levels (Floor 1 is ground level; floors are linked by the main stair, and each floor climbed adds about a minute):
  Undercroft: Workshop beneath the Lecture Halls; Archive beneath the Library, with the Restricted Section below it; the Seal Chamber deepest of all, reached only by the Warden's stair.
  Floor 1: Arbiter Hall (its vault rises through Floor 3), Ring Dining Hall, Canteen, Main Library reading rooms, Club Rooms corridor with the Student Council Chamber at its end and the Announcement Room off it, the Notice Board in the entrance hall at the foot of the main stair; the Warden's Office down its own corridor.
  Floor 2: first-year Lecture Halls, Portrait Hall gallery along the Arbiter Hall's upper level, Study Rooms on the Library's galleries.
  Floor 3: second-year Lecture Halls, Seminar Rooms, the Library's shadowed upper stacks.
  Floor 4: third-year Lecture Halls, the four Potion Halls at the base of their towers.
  Floor 5: Faculty Offices, Staff Room; the Headmaster's Office in its turret, up a short stair.
  Rooftop: flat lead roofs, the Bell Tower belfry, the Potion Hall tower tops.
  Lockers line the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor.
- Announcement Pillars (live broadcast from the Announcement Room) stand across the whole academy.
- Dormitories: Main Courtyard – Fire, Light, Sky and Viridian Dormitories, four separate buildings around it; each dormitory – its Common Room, Laundry, Bathhouse.
- Student life: Main Courtyard – The Mall, Mail Tower. The Mall – Medical Centre, Commissary (each its own building beside it), Banking House, Meditation Rooms/Spirit House.
- Outer grounds: Main Courtyard – Founder's Park, Combat Grounds, Sports Field, Gardens, Grassy Field/Hills. Founder's Park – Gardens, Sports Field. Sports Field – Gymnasium, Archery Range. Gymnasium – Swimming Pool (outdoor). Gardens – Menagerie. Hills – Observation Tower, Old Hut.
- Far edge: Gardens – Boathouse/Lake – Forest. Hills – Forest. Forest – Forest Clearing.
- Set apart from the core: the Dovecote, Cathedral, Royal Inspectorate and Noble Houses' Liaison stand together on one side of the grounds; between them and the Fire Dormitory, in the trees, stands the Broken Statue; the Detention Tower stands alone. All but the Detention Tower sit on academy land the academy does not control.
Club venues: Duelling – Combat Grounds; Soccer – Sports Field; Running, Walking – Hills; Gardening – Gardens; Beast Handling – Menagerie; Fishing – Lake; Alchemy, Brewing – Potion Halls; Smithing – Workshop; Library Assistants – Main Library; Warding Study – Seminar Rooms; Festival Committee – Council Chamber; Groundskeeping – Groundskeeper's Lodge; Cooking – Common Rooms; Medical Centre Volunteers – Medical Centre; Newspaper – Announcement Room; Music, Theatre, Card, Board Game, Divination, Tailoring, Drawing, Calligraphy, Tea, Specialized Magic – Club Rooms.
Walking times are measured FROM Main Courtyard, which is the navigation anchor, not a required stop: castle core and dormitories under 5 min; Mall and services 5; Founder's Park 5; Broken Statue 5; Combat Grounds and Sports Field 10; Gardens, Menagerie, Hills 15; Old Hut 20; Boathouse and Lake 20; Forest treeline 25; Forest Clearing 40.
Movement: adjacent places are reached directly, usually in four or five minutes. Characters do not pass through the Courtyard to reach a neighbour. Crossing between distant clusters does take real time; say so rather than skipping it.
The Gatehouse is the only way in or out. A dormitory admits only its own students.

W1 Mon Entrance Event. W3 Sat evening to Sun dawn Star Night. W4 Sat Spiritual Dorm Day.

135.content:

W1 Fri dusk to Sat dawn Warding Rite (whole academy renews the wards). W3 Wed-Fri Creature Studies Expedition (off-grounds, Grade III country).

136.content:

W1 Mon-Thu Midterm. W2 Fri-Sat Club Festival. W3 Mon-Sat Training Week (the one week cross-dorm sparring is allowed). W4 Sat-Sun Dorm Competition (solo, top 16 qualify).

137.content:
[Current month: Month 4]
W1 Wed Secret Fools Day (prank day, dorm name-draw). W2 Tue Independence Crowning Day (kingdom holiday, celebrated on campus). W3 Sat Mystic Dorm Day. W4 normal classes.

138.content:

139.content:
[Current month: Month 6]
W1 Mon-Fri Return Week. W3 Sat Sports Day (magic banned outright). W4 Wed-Sat Academy Competition (cross-dorm teams of 4).

140.content:
[Current month: Month 7]
W2 Magical & Science Fair. W3 Mon-Sun The Thinning: the seal is at its weakest, the academy is locked down for the week, nobody outside.

141.content:
[Current month: Month 8]
W2 Thu evening to Sun Traveling Circus visits. W3 Thu-Sat Academy Showcase. W4 Sat Elemental Dorm Day.

142.content:
[Current month: Month 9]
W1 Mon-Thu Midterm. W2 Thu-Sat Academy Bazaar. W3 Sat Academy Founder Day. W4 Thu-Sun Kingdom Competition (four academies, one team each).

143.content:
[Current month: Month 10]
W1 Tue Remembrance Day. W2 Sat Occult Dorm Day. W3 open. W4 Fri evening to Sun Harvest Festival.

144.content:
[Current month: Month 11]
W1 Mon-Thu End of Semester exams. W2 Fri Results & Final Ranking. W3 Mon-Wed Academy Trip (Sunreach Bay, abroad). W4 Sat Graduation.
