[Current month: Month 12]
Kingdom-wide holiday all month, students go home, campus nearly empty. W4 Thu-Sun World Competition, abroad.

201.content:
[Period Change]
Rule: when the bell ends a period, the main corridors are impassable for four minutes, then empty as fast as they filled.
Lateness: teachers time the Lecture Halls to Seminar Rooms walk to the minute; no excuse works.
Feel: crushing, deafening.

202.content:
[Skipping Class]
Spots: the boathouse, the far end of the Gardens, the dark upper stacks of the Main Library, the stairwells behind the Workshop.
Forest: the only real disappearance, so staff check it first.
Risk: an hour missing gets a slow walk to the Medical Centre; an afternoon means the hills, visible from the Bell Tower.

203.content:
[Exam Week]
Signs: the Main Library stays full at night; Study Rooms unbookable a fortnight ahead; the canteen serves whoever turns up whenever; daily mana exhaustion in the Medical Centre; Firetooth and Nightwell's Vigil as study currency; Star Cookies sold out before seven; Dragonchess boards gather dust.
Mood: everyone short with everyone, forgiven afterwards.

204.content:
[Assignments and Group Work]
Load: Magic Theory sets weekly written work; History sets essays nobody starts early; Creature Studies and Potion Crafting set assigned pair practicals, so students from different dorms end up owing each other favours; Combat sets no homework and everyone points it out.
Group work: the standard excuse for being anywhere at any hour; staff know how often it is true. Library tables and club rooms become meeting points near exams.

205.content:
[The Third Stall]
Where: one stall in every Bathhouse and Washroom block, always occupied, never answers.
Rule: knock twice and something knocks back; knock a third time and the latch opens on an empty stall. Never test it after the night bell.
Passed down as a senior's joke.

206.content:
[The Long Corridor]
Where: the castle's main corridor, walked alone after the night burn.
Story: it runs longer than by day, the same doors passing twice; no figure, only a walk that took eleven minutes when the bell says otherwise.
Told near the Bell Tower or after late Library sessions.

207.comment: Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
207.content:
[The Three O'Clock Knock]
Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.
Rule: three evenly spaced knocks; count them and go back to sleep. It is never four, and nobody wants to learn what four means.
Students argue whether sound can even cross the door wards.

208.comment: Ghost Story - The Crying on the Water
208.content:
[The Crying on the Water]
Where: the Lake, after dark. A woman crying, never close, never twice from the same direction; rowers hear it most, and no one has ever reached the sound.
Rule: boat bookings after sunset are refused, with a different reason every time.
The Fishing Club blames distance.

209.content:
[The Night Student]
Where: the Lecture Hall tier, after curfew. A student in an old-cut uniform crosses, sits, and waits for a class; accounts never agree on the dorm colour.
Mostly placed in the breach year, so third-years refuse to tell it. It resurfaces every Remembrance Day.

210.content:
[Sunfizz] The soda every student drinks, sold at the Commissary and the Mall store in heavy glass bottles.
Price: 8 points, 2 back per returned bottle.
Taste: absurdly sweet.
Known for: confiscated in lectures; caps litter the Lecture Halls.

211.content:
[The Lucky Roll] The Canteen's free filled roll, baked in batches, no two fillings alike, nothing written down.
Taste: mostly good; a few memorable for the wrong reasons, and the kitchen will not say what is in them.
Known for: eating one in front of an audience is a standing dare; unopened rolls are traded.

212.content:
[Ardenne] The luxury marque in magical equipment: focuses, instruments, cases, measuring tools. Run by the Ardenne family.
Price: an Ardenne focus is the 4,000-point tier; the cheapest item, a case, costs more than most students' monthly payout.
Known for: marks its owner instantly as wealthy; never advertises.

213.content:
[Firetooth] A tin of hard sweets hot enough to make the eyes water, sold everywhere.
Price: 12 points.
Known for: bought almost only in exam weeks on the theory that pain keeps you awake (disputed); sharing a tin in a Study Room at 2am is tradition; a nuisance to the Medical Centre.

214.content:
[Nightwell] A small Mall coffee house with one famous order, the Vigil.
Price: 60 points.
Known for: two days without sleep, paid for afterwards; the Medical Centre sees the results a day and a half later. Exam-week staple.

215.content:
[The Oracle Shell] A palm-sized novelty shell from the Mall that answers any spoken question with yes, no, or ask again later.
Price: 40 points.
Known for: transparently random, asked anyway, for jokes or 2am secrets. Real diviners find it insulting, which helps sales.

216.content:
[Merryhew's] The Mall's joke shop: itching charms, voice-changing sweets, illusion vermin, screaming boxes, fake exam results convincing enough to be banned twice.
Rules: tolerated because everything wears off; keeps a secret list of students barred from buying.

217.content:
[The Snug] A Mall eating house where every table is a partitioned private booth.
Known for: ordinary food, real privacy. Point loans, betting settlements, club trades, apologies and quiet negotiations; staff hear nothing. Booths by the hour, always a wait.

218.content:
[Dragonchess]
Play: starts as ordinary chess (drawn from chess and shogi) on floating checkered spheres over golden clockwork pedestals that materialise the pieces. The board reads the players and escalates: it unfolds into layers and the pieces fight autonomously in real time, so players outmanoeuvre both the opponent and the game.
Known for: rare sets; serious matches last days.

219.content: [Mana Grid] The academy runs on a grid drawn from the flow the seal already collects. It feeds the magic lanterns and the torches bracketed along the corridors and the perimeter: light that does not smoke, gutter, or leave its bracket. Draw peaks at month end and the lanterns visibly dim, which students read as a clock and complain about as weather. Nothing on the grid records or transmits anything; the Announcement Pillars are a separate sound working that only carries live voice. The Warden's Office monitors consumption rather than operating the grid itself, and the Bell Tower's first bell is the clearest daily sign that it is working.

221.content:
[Paid Work] Posts a student can take during term, all logged and all capped in hours so nobody earns near the top band.
- Canteen kitchen and serving: the most shifts and the least competition.
- Mail Tower sorting floor: heaviest on Sundays when the letters go out.
- Commissary counter: term start and exam weeks only.
- Library and archive shelving: quiet, sought after, and rarely advertised twice.
- Menagerie mucking out: pays the most because nobody wants it.
- Workshop repair: needs an actual skill and is paid accordingly.
- Potion Halls cleaning: supervised, strict disposal rules, good pay.
- Tutoring: arranged privately, paid in points or in favours.
Most posts pay twenty to forty points a shift. Openings go up on the Notice Board and are gone within a day. Groundskeeping and Library Assistants are clubs, not posts, and members are not paid.

222.content:
[Star Cookie] A star-shaped bakery biscuit.
Price: 8 points.
Rule: eaten whole, in one go, before anything that matters (an exam, a duel, a confession). Halves do not count.
Known for: the bakery sells out by seven on exam mornings and never increases the batch, which students treat as part of it.

223.content:
[The Founder's Hand]
Rule: touch the Founder's Statue's outstretched hand before an exam, always the hand, always on the way out.
Known for: the hand is polished bright while the rest is green; a queue every exam morning, even from non-believers.

224.content:
[Sleeping in the Library]
Story: fall asleep over a book and you wake somewhere else: a reading room with the wrong number of doors, shelves out of order, nobody else in the building.
Rule: sit still and sleep again; do not walk. Everyone who tells it woke the second time in their own chair.
Known for: late revisers go in pairs; staff clear the reading rooms at the night bell without explaining why.

225.content:
[Eating in the Forest]
Rule: share first. Leave a bite on the ground or a crust on a stump before the first mouthful.
Known for: Creature Studies says it only feeds foxes; students do it anyway, and anyone who eats everything hears about it.

226.content:
[Taken]
Story: what came through the Crack takes people by their names.
Rule: outdoors after dark, never answer to your own name unless you can see who called. Students walking back near curfew call each other by dorm, club, or nothing.
Status: nobody claims it has happened; everybody obeys it, especially near the Bell Tower and Forest edge.

229.content:
[Magical Beasts - Name List]
Grades: IV nuisance, III dangerous to a person, II dangerous to a group, I settlement-scale. Students handle nothing above III, except third-years on the Creature Studies Expedition. Vary the creature to the place; do not default to boars.
MENAGERIE (IV): giant rat, dire rabbit, fire salamander, frost weasel, glow moth, thunder beetle, rock snail, copper quill hedgehog, ember toad, stone lizard, mana leech, chittering bat, spark finch, pocket drake, cave newt, horned goat, iron mole, lesser slime, imp.
GROUNDS AND GARDENS (IV): thorn creeper, pollen wasp, mandrake, shriek mushroom, hedge serpent, brass beetle, chimney sootcat, bell mite, rootling, garden shrike.
LAKE: giant carp, river eel, snapping turtle (IV); giant crayfish, lake serpent, kelpie, merrow (III).
FOREST, academy and grand alike (III): dire wolf, boar, thornstag, giant spider, giant centipede, owlbear. Grand forest only: goblin hound (IV), harpy, forest troll, ashen lynx, mist wolf, lesser drake, cockatrice, gargoyle (III).
GRAND FOREST (II, expedition and hunting country): basilisk, manticore, wyvern, chimera, griffin, ogre, cave troll, dire bear, young hydra, giant scorpion, ironback boar, cinder wyrm, dread weaver, bone drake, roc, displacer cat, gorgon, rime elk.
DISTANT AND LEGENDARY (I, never on academy grounds): dragon, ancient wyrm, elder hydra, leviathan, behemoth, giant, kraken, sphinx, the Sablemaw, the Gaunt Herd.
PROTECTED, killing or harming one is a crime the Doves investigate: unicorn, kirin, phoenix, hippogriff, lantern stag, grey pilgrim, moonhare, white hart, sun crane, hearthcat, pearl serpent. Deep forest and remote country; Halvard's Menagerie holds none. Poaching has its own black market and hunting companies refuse the work.

230.content:
[Creature Studies Expedition]
When: Month 2 Week 3, Wednesday to Friday. The Creature Studies practical exam, run by the Creature Studies teachers, one per year level, with the first-year teacher (the ex-monster hunter) leading.
Where: the Grand Vast Forest, half a day by airship; one ship per year level.
Teams: groups of four, graded together.
Wed: flight, then camp (tents, cookfires, watch rotations) and gear prep.
Thu: each group is assigned a beast to bring back within 24 hours. Years 1-2 get Grade III targets, year 3 Grade II. Staff shadow at a distance and pull out groups in trouble.
Fri: break camp, fly home. Catches count dead or alive.
Marking: identification, handling and teamwork over kills; a clean capture beats a messy one.

231.content:
[Airships]
Use: the kingdom's long-distance transport, hired by the academy for anything past a day's ride: the Expedition, the Academy Trip, the long breaks, travel to the Kingdom and World Competitions.
Onboard: big enough to live on; glassed promenade, common room, canteen, washrooms and bathing stalls, one cabin per group of four; cargo, gear and beast pens below.
Crew: hired, not academy staff. Teachers take the forward cabins and count passengers at boarding and landing. Nothing aboard records or sends anything.

232.content:
[Midterm]
When: Month 3 Week 1 and Month 9 Week 1, Monday to Thursday. Normal classes stop for the week.
Mon: Magic Theory, then Etiquette. Written.
Tue: History written; Potion Crafting practical (one brew from a sealed brief, marked on result and process).
Wed: Dark Magic Defense practical, each student against the teacher. Nobody is expected to win; the mark is for how long you hold.
Thu: Combat practical, students paired within their year, marked by combat role.
Creature Studies sits no midterm; it is marked on fieldwork.
Marks post at week's end; dorm ranking waits for end-of-semester results. In Month 9, Magic Theory may be replaced by a Magical & Science Fair score.

233.content:
[Club Festival]
When: Month 3 Week 2, Friday afternoon and all of Saturday.
What: every club runs a stand in the Main Courtyard: demonstrations, displays, contests, food. Duelling and sport clubs run exhibition matches, Alchemy and Smithing sell their work, Beast Handling brings out tame specimens, quieter clubs use displays and free samples. Club-funded, staffed in shifts.
Voting: every student and staff member gets one gold coin to drop at the best stand; nobody votes for their own club, advisors included. Winner announced at Saturday's close.
Prize: prestige only, plus better leverage for room space and budget all year.

234.content:
[Training Week]
When: Month 3 Week 3, Monday to Saturday, the week before the Dorm Competition.
Classes run normally. Curfew moves to 9pm and the Combat Grounds, duelling rings and practice halls stay open and supervised into the evening.
Taking part is optional. Students spar, drill and test builds against each other, freely across years and dorms.

235.content:
[Secret Fools Day]
When: Month 4 Week 1, Wednesday.
Dorm draw: each dorm has a box of its members' names. Participants draw one in secret and prank that person without warning, so everyone suspects everyone all day.
Campus-wide: Merryhew's biggest sale of the year; unclaimed pranks and decorations everywhere.
Classes still run and nothing is learned; some teachers prank their own students.
Limits: nothing that injures, nothing touching wards, specimen pens or the Potion Halls. The Doves ignore it unless something causes real damage.

236.content:
[End of Semester Exams]
When: Month 5 Week 1 and Month 11 Week 1, Monday to Thursday. No classes; one exam and nothing else.
Form: a single practical trial covering every subject, taken alone, one student at a time (hence four days). The course is rebuilt between runs.
The run, in order: a sealed door opened only by solving a theory problem (Magic Theory); a beast to identify and get past, not kill (Creature Studies); unlabelled ingredients and a condition to treat (Potion Crafting); a cursed room to cross and leave clean (Dark Magic Defense); an examiner in role who has to be talked around without magic or threats, with history cited as proof (Etiquette, History); a duel against a staff member, marked by the student's combat role (Combat).
Marking: stage by stage; failing a stage does not end the run, and almost nobody clears all six. Royal Inspectorate examiners watch from the gallery.

237.content:
[Results & Dorm Ranking]
When: Month 5 Week 2 Friday and Month 11 Week 2 Friday.
Arbiter Hall assembly: trial results given stage by stage, then the dorm ranking is recalculated from every member's marks and read aloud last. It holds until the next ranking day.
Evening: feast in the Ring Dining Hall.
Mood: one dorm celebrates, three eat anyway.

238.content:
[Mid-Year Break]
When: Month 5 Week 4, Monday to Sunday. No classes, no clubs.
Airships leave the first morning and return the last. Staying is allowed and common (far provinces, nowhere to go, or simply wanting the week). The canteen runs short hours and half the mall closes. A skeleton staff and the Warden stay to keep the seal fed.
Mood: quiet enough to hear the bells from anywhere.

239.content:
[Sports Day]
When: Month 6 Week 3, Saturday. No classes, no club block.
Rule: magic banned in every event; the one day a powerful mage counts for nothing.
Events: optional, open to anyone; most of the academy watches. Sports Field for running and team events, Main Courtyard for crowd contests, the lake and Combat Grounds for the rest. Sport clubs supply most favourites.
Medals: gold, silver, copper per event, tallied by dorm at day's end. Bragging rights for a year; no effect on dorm ranking.

240.content:
[Magical & Science Fair]
When: Month 7 Week 2, Friday and Saturday. Run by the first-year Magic Theory teacher.
What: stands in the Main Courtyard, solo or any group size: inventions, research, demonstrations, anything where magic meets science. Built through the week; Friday set-up and viewing, Saturday judging.
Judging: a staff panel questions and scores each stand. A student may use that score as their Month 9 Magic Theory midterm mark instead of the written paper. Group stands share one score.
Range: genuinely useful to spectacular nonsense; the panel has rewarded both.

241.content:
[Traveling Circus]
When: Month 8 Week 2, Thursday evening to Sunday. A hired touring company, not an academy event.
What: a great tent in the Main Courtyard with several shows a day; stands, games, sideshows and fortune tellers across the grounds. Stalls take points.
Rules: classes run Friday and Saturday morning; curfew moves to 10pm.
Doves: dislike and monitor the large group of outsiders. Half the show is real magic, half stagecraft, and the performers will not say which.
Mood: the whole campus turned carnival.

242.content:
[Academy Showcase]
When: Month 8 Week 3, Thursday to Saturday.
What: the Main Courtyard becomes a stage; students perform solo or in groups (music, dance, spectacle casting, comedy). Optional; acts run all three days.
Judging: a panel scores every act; scores tallied by dorm on Saturday to name the most talented dorm. Bragging rights only.
Visitors: parents and guardians invited, logged at the Gatehouse; the mall's best trading days.
Mood: students manage their families as much as they perform; those with nobody coming are careful how they say so.

243.content:
[Academy Bazaar]
When: Month 9 Week 2, Thursday to Saturday.
What: invited traders from the capital, the provinces and abroad fill the Main Courtyard; the academy takes a cut. Stock the mall never carries: foreign sweets and drink, charms, imported components, odd instruments, foreign fashion, items nobody can explain.
Prices: whatever the trader says; haggling expected; stalls take points. A year's savings can vanish in an afternoon.
Security: traders logged at the Gatehouse; the Doves watch the stock and the crowd.

244.content:
[Remembrance Day]
When: Month 10 Week 1, Tuesday. A Halvard day, not a kingdom one, marking the breach night two years ago.
Rules: nothing loud (no clubs, duelling, music, games, sport); classes run quietly; the Bell Tower keeps a slow pattern. Bouquets line the halls until evening.
Honoured: the students killed that night and the Warden who died resealing the Crack. The Acting Warden attends and is not asked to speak.
Evening: lantern release on the Grassy Field and Hills, one lantern per person.
Mood: memory for third-years, inherited for everyone else; silent until the last lantern is gone.

245.content:
[Harvest Festival]
When: Month 10 Week 4, Friday evening to Sunday. The largest festival of the year, the last loud thing before exams.
What: clubs, dorm floors and year groups run cafés, food stalls, game booths, haunted houses in the older corridors, and small stage acts. Nothing judged, no tally.
Costume: students and half the staff dress as monsters, ghosts and beasts, masks included; the cheaper and sillier the better. Carved lanterns line every path.
Visitors: families invited all three days, logged at the Gatehouse.
Rules: curfew 11pm Friday and Saturday.
Close: Sunday fireworks over the lake, watched from the Grassy Field and Hills.

246.content:
[Sunreach Bay]
What: a small island and coastal nation, the world's playground, half a day from Halvard by airship.
Day: paradise; white beaches, turquoise lagoons, wholesome family fun.
Night: neon casinos, pleasure houses, every vice sold openly.
Policy: gives you whatever you came for and asks no questions.

247.content:
[Academy Trip]
When: Month 11 Week 3, Monday to Wednesday. All three years; the third-years' last event as students.
Where: Sunreach Bay, half a day by airship. Whole beachfront hotels booked, four to a room; the rest is free time.
Rules: teachers in the same hotels set a curfew; leave the hotel only in groups of four. The day side is allowed; the night side is out of bounds, which some students ignore every year.
Money: points do not work abroad; this is what a year of saving is for, and Sunreach is expensive.
Mood: students return tired, sunburnt and poorer than planned.

248.content:
[Graduation]
When: Month 11 Week 4, Saturday. Third-years leave; everyone attends.
Morning: Arbiter Hall ceremony. The Headmaster speaks, dorm heads read out their graduates, and each touches the Arbiter Stone a second and last time, the only time anyone touches it twice. Families, nobles and the Noble Houses' Liaison sit in the gallery.
Afternoon: recruitment tables from noble houses, the Royal Inspectorate, the Dovecote, the Bank, hunting companies and city guilds, courting graduates they have tracked for three years. Offers made and refused on the spot.
Evening: feast; graduates leave by airship the next morning.

249.content:
[Spirit Pact]
A negotiated contract: both sides must agree, a spirit cannot be forced, and the terms can be anything the two settle on. Two uses:
Channelling (Greater and Spirit Lord only): the spirit's ability used without summoning it. Costs mana per use and comes through far weaker than the spirit's own.
Summoning (any tier): the spirit drains mana the whole time it is present, more the stronger it is, and more again for every ability it uses. Killed in combat, it takes an hour to a week to call back depending on the mage.

253.content:
[Combat Roles]
Five roles used in Combat Class, exams and team competitions. A student may fill more than one.
- Attack: deals the damage and finishes fights.
- Defense: shields, blocks and holds the line for the team.
- Healing: keeps allies standing mid-fight.
- Support: strengthens allies and weakens enemies.
- Control: restrains, disrupts and shapes the battlefield.

254.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Forest Clearing
254.content:
[Forest Clearing] A single oak called the Elder Oak stands in an open clearing in the middle of the Forest, so broad a dozen students holding hands cannot circle it, and older than the castle by anyone's guess. The canopy opens above the clearing, so the oak stands in full sun while the woods around it stay dim; the muffled quiet of the Forest gives way to birdsong at its edge, and gold motes drift in the light even on grey days. Its roots pull the ground's mana into slow currents unlike anywhere else on campus, and a wild field of rare flowers has spread across the clearing around it, in colours found nowhere else. The Gardening Club has tried transplanting them; they wilt within a day of leaving the clearing. A deer path leads in from the treeline, about fifteen minutes' walk. Students come to read, nap between the roots, or be alone without feeling lost. The crust for Eating in the Forest goes on its roots. Patrols turn students back at dusk, and nobody answers their name out here after dark.
Feel: sunlit, still, majestic, flower-scent and birdsong.

255.content:
[Rooftop] The flat lead roofs of the castle core, joined by parapet walks and short stairs between the gables. Officially out of bounds. The only way up is a small locked door off the Bell Tower stair, and the trick of opening it is passed from older students to younger ones, never written down; being shown the way up means someone has decided you belong. From the parapet the whole academy lies open: the courtyards, the four dormitories, the Hills, the Lake, the Forest's dark edge, the white roofs of the Dovecote. At night the mana lanterns spread below like a lit map, and at month end you can watch them dim together. The campus's quiet romantic secret: couples come up for sunset and the lantern view, and a hidden corner behind the eastern gable is where confessions happen. Nobody who has been brought up here tells, and the rule is to leave a corner free if someone is already in it. Birds lift off just before each bell, and the lead hums underfoot when it rings. Staff walk the courtyards after curfew, never the roof.
Feel: wide sky, wind, sun-warm lead, a shared secret.

256.content:
[Headmaster's Office] At the end of the Faculty Offices corridor, a round room up a short stair, its tall windows over the Main Courtyard. Forty years of one Elf's tenure fill it: shelves layered deep with books, and letters and small gifts from graduates. In the window stands a sapling grown from the Elder Oak, forty years old and still knee-high. Students come only when it matters: serious discipline, a request to repeat a year, news no one wants to hear. The bench outside is where the real waiting happens. Visitors from the Royal Inspectorate and the Dovecote are received here, since the Headmaster has no authority inside their walls. The door stands open whenever the Headmaster is in.
Feel: old wood, ink, green leaves, patient quiet.

257.content:
[Romantic Spots]
Spots: the Rooftop at sunset or under the lantern view, for those who have been shown the way up; the flower field around the Elder Oak in the Forest Clearing by day; the willow island on the Lake, rowed out to at dusk before the boathouse stops taking bookings, then watched glowing with fireflies from the shore; a booth at the Snug; the quieter back paths of Founder's Park.
Favourite date events: Star Night, the classic confession under the midnight meteor shower on the Hills; the Harvest Festival, walking lantern-lined paths in matching costumes and watching the Sunday fireworks over the lake together; the Traveling Circus, the big tent, the stalls and a fortune teller read for two; the Academy Trip, the beach at Sunreach Bay by day.

258.content:
[Staff Quarters] A separate stone house for the resident teaching staff (Dorm Heads live in their own dormitories instead), standing on its own beside the castle and joined to the castle's ground floor by a short covered walk: private rooms upstairs, and downstairs a shared parlour with mismatched armchairs, a kettle that is never cold, and a porch facing the Gardens. Where the Staff Room keeps students out, the Staff Quarters let them in: students may knock until the eight o'clock bell, and nothing said in the parlour counts as a consultation or a referral. It is where students come for help they would not ask for in class, advice about home, a second opinion on a club, or just tea with a teacher they like. Teachers here are off duty and act like it. Every door says something about who lives behind it: forest air draughting under Gavlan's, two teacups and a stack of theory on Layla's, and notes slid under Mimosa's, answered by morning. Vallie Goredust lives out by the Menagerie but holds court in the parlour anyway.
Feel: lamplight, tea, worn armchairs, lived-in.

259.content:
[Fire Dormitory] Home of the Elementalists (red vest). Red-tiled roof and a red banner over the door. A great hearth burns in its common room day and night, and the broad chimney stack rising above the front of the building is always warm, even in winter. Inside: a common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Through the Elements, Victory Is Ours."
Feel: hearth warmth, woodsmoke, stone.

260.content:
[Light Dormitory] Home of the Mystics (yellow vest). Golden-tiled roof and a yellow banner over the door. Its inner court is roofed by a glass dome over the common area, which glows from within after dark. Inside: the glass dome common area plus personal rooms. Creed: "The Third Eye Lights The Way."
Feel: sunlight through glass, pale stone.

261.content:
[Sky Dormitory] Home of the Occultists (blue vest). Deep-blue-tiled roof and a blue banner over the door. A single slender tower rises from one corner, and the building's enchanted walls let residents see the academy grounds from their rooms; from outside the windows shimmer faintly, like water. Inside: common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Together We Are Strong."
Stigma: Occult carries a reputation no other type does. Outsiders associate it with blood magic, demon summoning, and spirits bound against their will, and cannot always tell legal Occult practice from forbidden work. The Doves watch Occultists more closely than any other dorm, and Sky students are often the first suspected when something goes wrong. The creed reflects this: Sky students close ranks because few others will stand with them.
Feel: cool stone, shimmering windows.

262.content:
[Viridian Dormitory] Home of the Spiritualists (green vest). Green-tiled roof and a green banner over the door. An old oak fills its inner court, its crown rising above the roofline, with meditation stones set among its roots. Inside: common area, meditation rooms, personal rooms. Creed: "Know Thyself, Know Victory."
Feel: oak shade, rustling leaves, stone.

263.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Old Hut
263.content:
[Old Hut] A one-room timber hut on the far slope of the Hills, where the grass runs out against the Forest treeline. Nobody remembers who built it or when; the Groundskeeper's Lodge lists it as disused and not worth repairing, and leaves it standing. The roof sags, the door hangs from one hinge, and the cold hearth still holds old ash. It is where students go to share secrets: far from every building and path, with nobody walking past, and by long student custom what is said inside the Old Hut stays there. Generations of confessions have left initials carved into the inside walls. It also serves as shelter from sudden rain, and on Star Night it is claimed before sunset. After dark nobody lingers, since it sits right on the Forest edge where patrols walk and names are not answered.
Feel: weathered wood, wind through gaps, grass and pine.

264.comment: Academy Location - Student Life - Announcement Room
264.content:
[Announcement Room] A small booth-like room off the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, home of the Academy Newspaper club. A speaking rune set into the desk carries whatever is said into it, live, to the Announcement Pillars around the grounds; nothing is recorded. Students on duty open the day with a good-morning after the seven o'clock bell and give the noon, afternoon and evening greetings, the last just before the eight o'clock bell. In between they read out what staff, the Student Council and event organisers send down, plus whatever the student on duty decides is important, the most argued-about power any club holds. Outside class periods the Music Club plays live from the side room, and the whole campus hears it. Staff can take over the rune for anything urgent; during The Thinning lockdown it is how the academy speaks to everyone at once.
Feel: cramped, warm lamplight, sheet music and newsprint.

265.content: [Announcement Pillars] Slender stone pillars carved with sound runes, standing across the whole academy. They carry the live voice or music from the Announcement Room and nothing else: they cannot be spoken into, record nothing, and are a separate working from the mana grid. Their runes glow faintly while a broadcast is live. They stay quiet during class periods except for urgent notices, and fall silent at curfew. None stand in the Forest or on the land of the outside powers, which is part of why those places feel so quiet.

266.comment: Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Broken Statue
266.content:
[Broken Statue] A white marble statue standing in a stand of old trees between the Fire Dormitory and the Dovecote, off the path students take when they would rather not walk past the Dovecote's front. The figure has lost its head and one arm; the arm lies half-sunk in the moss at its feet, and moss and lichen have crept over the rest until the white shows only in patches. The inscription on its plinth has worn smooth. Who it depicted is unknown, and nobody on staff claims to know; students have theories and none of them agree. Groundskeeping leaves it exactly as it is. Light comes through the leaves in pieces, and the place is quieter than it should be for somewhere so close to the courtyard.
Feel: green shade, cold marble, moss, stillness.
<narrator_only>A hidden room lies beneath the statue. During The Thinning a low growl rises from under the plinth, faint enough to pass for wind in the trees from the Fire Dormitory windows nearest the grove.</narrator_only>
